opinions.rationale: The central warning is valid and potentially high severity: handling death or another intercurrent event is part of defining the estimand, and total, controlled direct, and separable effects answer different questions. The entry is nevertheless conceptually imprecise. An estimand is defined by its counterfactual outcomes and contrast; identification assumptions are separate. Simply censoring at death does not select or identify one of those causal effects. Depending on the analysis, it can instead produce a cause-specific risk-set quantity or an unidentified hypothetical contrast. The claims that censoring is normally silent and that recurrent and terminal events are seldom modeled jointly are empirical frequency claims not established by the cited package source. Pinned lmtp source exports lmtp_tmle, lmtp_sdr, and lmtp_survival; accepts longitudinal treatment, censoring, and competing-risk nodes; incorporates competing-event status in its recursion; and tests two treatment times with two competing-risk times. Pinned gfoRmula source exports gformula_survival and static and implements sustained intervention risks with an explicit competing-event model and an option governing whether that event is treated as censoring. These implementations address competing risks under longitudinal strategies, but neither exposes an explicit joint recurrent-event and terminal-event estimand. The narrower implementation and protocol gap therefore remains.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Death and other competing or intercurrent events must be handled explicitly in the target estimand and protocol. Treating a competing event as censoring changes the observed-data analysis and can support a hypothetical elimination estimand only when the intervention is well defined and its identification conditions hold; censoring alone does not select or identify a total, controlled direct, or separable effect. Explicit off-the-shelf support remains limited for joint recurrent-event and terminal-event contrasts under sustained longitudinal strategies.

resolving_work.title: lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: The pinned NAMESPACE exports lmtp_tmle, lmtp_sdr, and lmtp_survival. The source accepts treatment variables ordered over time together with censoring and competing-risk indicators, and its fidelity test applies repeated treatment and competing-risk nodes. This supplies estimators for cumulative incidence under longitudinal treatment policies, but not an explicit joint recurrent-terminal contrast.
